name: ShopCursor_Advance
algorithm: Advances a struct ShopCursor's animation by one frame. Guards on cursor!=NULL and cursor->kind!=0 (kind doubles as the animation's total frame count). Increments cursor->active (the elapsed-frame counter), then for each axis linearly interpolates: new = axisStart + FixedPoint_Ratio(active * (axisTarget - axisStart), kind), writing the X result to anchor->x (offset 6) and merging its low 9 bits into anchor+22 (preserving the existing high 7 bits), and writing the Y result to anchor->y (offset 8) and anchor+20 as a truncated byte. anchor is cursor->anchor (offset 0). When active reaches kind, both cursor->kind and cursor->active are reset to 0, ending the animation.
evidence: struct ShopCursor (games/gs1/include/shop.h) already declares anchor@0, x@4(u16), y@6(u16), target_x@8(s16), target_y@10(s16), active@12(s8), kind@13(s8), size 0x10 -- an exact, unforced match for this owner's six field offsets and overall frame size, independently established by the already-adopted games/gs1/src/shop/set_cursor_position.c (Shop_SetCursorPosition), which constructs the same struct from a 'kind' parameter and zeroes 'active' at animation start.

The immediately following owner, main:080b0958 (named ShopCursor_MoveTowardTarget in games/gs1/source-paths.json, not yet source-adopted), starts exactly at this owner's end address (0x080b08b8 + 0xa0 = 0x080b0958) and operates on the same anchor object: it reads/writes anchor->x (offset 6) and anchor->y (offset 8), and merges anchor+22 with an identical 'AND 0x1ff / AND 0xfffffe00 / OR' idiom against literal-pool constants 0x0000ffff/0x000001ff/0xfffffe00, plus truncates anchor->y into anchor+20 as a byte -- byte-for-byte the same bitfield-preserve pattern this owner uses on the same four anchor offsets. MoveTowardTarget is a proportional ease-toward-target mover (step = (target-current)/4, clamped, no frame counter); this owner is architecturally different -- a keyframed linear tween driven by an explicit active/kind frame counter -- so it is named as a sibling ShopCursor_* verb rather than reusing MoveTowardTarget's name.

Func_080022ec (called twice, both times as the second positional argument after the interpolation product) is already declared and named FixedPoint_Ratio/Math_Div throughout games/gs1/include/types.h and battle_calc.h, and games/gs1/src/display/blend/update_transition.c shows the identical 'level = start + FixedPoint_Ratio(delta * step, total)' idiom this owner reproduces per-axis.
